Subject: Clarification: audit history exportability & tamper-evidence requirements

Hi Michael,

Thanks for the materials you sent last week. Our security team reviewed Redwood's audit log capabilities and had a few follow-ups before we finalize the RFP response. Two priority items:

1) Bulk extract SLA: we require capability to produce a complete account-level audit-history export (inclusive of admin actions, API calls, and rendered model outputs metadata) within 72 hours. Please confirm your standard SLA and any options for expedited delivery.

2) Tamper evidence and chain-of-custody: we need proof that exported audit data is tamper-evident and can be cryptographically verified by our auditors. Examples we like: signed manifests, hash-chain proofs, and an immutable sequence ID.

Also attached is a sample manifest format our audit team will use — can you indicate whether Redwood can produce this natively or provide a mapping?

Best,
Sanjay

Hi Sanjay — thanks for the clear asks and the sample manifest. High-level responses below; Laura is looping in product engineering to add the fine-grained export mapping.

1) Bulk extract SLA: our standard response window for full account-level audit exports is 48-72 hours depending on size. For enterprise Dedicated/Private customers we offer a 24-hour expedited SLA as an add-on (contracted). We can commit to 48 hours for Aegis under the proposed Dedicated plan; if you need 24-hour guaranteed delivery we can add that to the SOW and incur an expedited delivery fee.

2) Tamper evidence & chain-of-custody: Redwood supports an append-only audit ledger for all control-plane and inference-event metadata. For exports we can provide:
- Signed manifest (JSON) with export_id, generated_by, timestamp, total_events, and root_hash (SHA-256). The manifest is signed with Redwood's export signing key and we provide the public key for verifier use.
- Event-level hashes and prev_hash linking (hash-chain) so auditors can verify ordering and detect insertion/deletion.
- Optional customer-side HMAC where we compute an HMAC using a customer-provided key in KMS during export to provide an additional tamper-proofing layer.

We can produce your manifest fields natively; Laura will confirm field name mappings and the exact payload_hash algorithm (we default to SHA-256).

Attachments: redwood-audit-export-sla.pdf (PDF stub; SLA options and turnaround times)

Next steps: Laura will post a mapping matrix in the shared doc and propose a sample export (NDJSON + manifest) for you to validate.

Thanks,
Michael
Head of Customer Security
Redwood Inference

--- Message 3 (technical mapping from engineering) ---
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay.rao@aegisinsurance.com>, Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Clarification: audit history exportability & tamper-evidence requirements

Hi Sanjay,

Following up with the mapping and technical details you asked for. We validated your sample manifest and can produce exports that match it with minimal translation. Key details: 

Export formats supported (you can choose per-export):
- NDJSON (newline-delimited JSON) — default, streaming-friendly, easy ingest into SIEMs
- Parquet — columnar, compressed, recommended for very large historical stores

Manifest and tamper-evidence specifics: 
- payload_hash: SHA-256 over the canonicalized JSON of the event payload (we canonicalize by stable key ordering and UTF-8 normalization).
- prev_hash: each event record includes prev_hash linking to the previous event's payload_hash, forming a chain.
- root_hash: we publish a merkle-root of the export bundle as well as the final chain tail hash for easy spot-checking.
- signature: manifest is signed with an RSA PSS 4096 key. We also support ECDSA (P-256) signatures on request.

Chain-of-custody and proofs: 
- We can generate a signed export manifest plus a detached proof file containing a sampling of per-event proofs for auditors.
- For longer retention windows where you require immutable proof, we can optionally notarize export roots to an external timestamping service (RFC 3161) at export time.

Retention and retention-triggered export: 
- Account-level audit retention default: 2 years on Hosted plan, 7 years on Dedicated/Private if requested (configurable in contract).
- We support on-demand bulk handoffs and periodic snapshots (monthly/quarterly). Snapshots include incremental deltas (sequence_id ranges) for bandwidth-efficient transfers.

Delivery and transfer options: 
- Push to your S3 bucket (pre-signed multipart uploads) — recommended for large exports.
- Temporary secure SFTP endpoint with client-cert auth.
- Encrypted archive delivered via customer-managed KMS (AES-256 wrapped by your KMS key).

Performance notes: for accounts with >5M events/day we use concurrent export workers and manifest sharding; typical 48-hour exports for multi-month windows are routable within the SLA. If you can share approximate event volume for the target retention window we will run a pre-flight estimate.

Mapping to your sample manifest: yes — sequence_id -> sequence_id (string), event_time -> event_time (ISO-8601), event_type -> event_type, actor -> actor.principal, resource -> resource.id, payload_hash -> payload_hash(SHA-256), prev_hash -> prev_hash. We will post a one-page mapping table in the shared doc.

Let us know if you need an NDA'd snapshot or a redacted sample before giving us production access.

Thanks,
Laura
Principal Product Manager, Observability
Redwood Inference

If you can post the verification runbook and a redacted sample (even synthetic) in the shared doc we can move this to procurement signoff next week.
